column5:
One of the most well-known climbs in the Dolomites and frequently used in the Giro d'Italia. It starts in the popular basecamp village of Cortina d'Ampezzo and takes on the more scenic northeast side of the climb in perfect autumn conditions. The first part of the climb shares the same road as the Passo Falzarego, which is available in the film collection as an alternative route that you could take from the 6 km mark.

The climb comes in two parts: the first part of 8km being fairly easy as you climb out of the valley to a light plateau to catch your breath. On the way, we catch a strong local rider who joins us for some miles. The main climb starts a little way after you have pulled off the more busy road to the Falzarego. It’s a mix of pine forests and opens up towards the top to some of the most amazing views in Europe. The profile is fairly uneven with some short steep sections. The Passo Fedaia would be the next climb if you were to descend all the way down the other side. This climb with its deep Sottoguda gorge is also available in the Tacx Collection.

A complete lap of the Forggensee lake in Germany on mainly car-free rolling cycleways and tracks. It has some wonderful mountain views with only a few very short steep parts which makes this a nice ride for everyone. The early part of the ride features some single tracks next to the lakeside, then the ride starts to become more undulating as it heads to the dam at the Lechsee in the northern end of the route. The final part features the only two hills that are long enough to be worth highlighting. Once at the top it's a nice roller coaster descent back to the start.

An early morning City trip round the landmarks of one of the finest city's in Italy especially famous for its incredible food & medieval towers. We start just outside the city to the north & ride in via cycle paths to the center. After about 15 completely flat kilometres the ride take a rather brutally sudden change as we take on the steep 2km climb to the cathedral of Madonna di San Luca. This steep climb which can easily be skipped has been immortalized by the haunting image of Fiorenzo Magni racing a time trial with a broken collarbone on San Luca in the 1956 Giro..

Workout tip - take the City as a nice light warm up, raise the pace in the 2km before the San Luca climb & then go for it. Dont go too hard at the start of the climb where it seems steep remember to save something for the mid way point where you cross to the other side of the covered walk way it reaches 20% here! 

For those that are not so fit please adjust the difficulty slider at the top right (the cog wheels) or in the settings before you get to the climb as its rather steep directly & you cant get off a walk! Alternatively just ride the two flat City rides & avoid this citys local challenge.

Taking in many of the climbs from the most popular classic in the cycling calendar: the Monument of Flanders. This is the second stage of a two-part ride starting in Kluisbergen and it tackles the lesser-known climbs that are often featured towards the start of the hilly part of the race. Like the cobbled Molenberg which is often featured in the tough Spring Classic's opener De Omloop. Staying mostly on the smaller more scenic signposted tourist route, this ride will give you a glimpse of the Flanders hills as seen in late summer sun. This stage features the final 10km on the quiet eastern bank of the Schelde river.

Included climbs: Heirweg, Foreest, Steenberg, Valkenberg and Molenberg.

Tip - To make an extra-long ride you could select to ride the 32km long Schelde River to Kluisbergen as a warm-up prior to stage 1 to get you a ride of about 100km.
